questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which semantic HTML5 element represents self-contained, independent composition content like a blog post or news item?
questions.explanation: An <article> represents an independent, reusable composition meant for standalone distribution.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which semantic HTML5 element represents content indirectly related to main content (like a sidebar)?
questions.explanation: <aside> defines content tangentially related to content around it (e.g., sidebars, callout boxes).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML5 tag wraps the dominant, central content unique to a specific document (excluding headers/footers)?
questions.explanation: <main> contains the main body of content unique to that document.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML5 input type provides a built-in interactive date picker in supporting browsers?
questions.explanation: <input type="date"> creates an input field with a native browser date picker UI.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which input attribute defines a regular expression pattern that the input value must match for validation?
questions.explanation: The 'pattern' attribute takes a JavaScript regex that user input is validated against.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML5 tag provides a pre-defined auto-complete list of options for an <input> field using the 'list' attribute?
questions.explanation: <datalist> contains <option> tags offering autocomplete choices for linked <input> elements.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: What is the purpose of ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes like `role` or `aria-label`?

options.B: To improve accessibility for users of assistive technologies like screen readers
options.D: To optimize search engine indexing speed

questions.explanation: ARIA attributes provide semantic accessibility metadata to assistive technology users.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: How should decorative images (images that carry no informational value) be marked for accessibility?
questions.explanation: An empty alt attribute (alt="") signals screen readers to skip purely decorative images.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which attribute in <video> or <audio> tags causes media to play automatically when page loads?
questions.explanation: The 'autoplay' boolean attribute requests instant playback upon media readiness.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which attribute displays browser default playback controls (play, pause, volume) on <video> elements?
questions.explanation: The 'controls' attribute displays standard native media control UI elements.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What does the `async` attribute do when executing external `<script src="app.js" async>`?

options.A: Fetches script in parallel and executes it immediately as soon as it downloads, non-blocking parsing
options.B: Defers execution until DOM parsing complete

questions.explanation: The 'async' attribute downloads the script asynchronously and runs it as soon as available, potentially before DOM completion.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What does the `defer` attribute do when loading external `<script src="app.js" defer>`?

options.B: Downloads script in parallel and executes it after DOM parsing finishes in document order

questions.explanation: The 'defer' attribute downloads script concurrently but delays execution until HTML parsing completes entirely.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What is the relationship between the <head> and <body> elements in an HTML document?

options.A: They are sibling elements contained inside <html>

questions.explanation: <head> and <body> are sibling children directly under the <html> root element.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What is the correct format for creating custom data attributes in HTML5?
questions.explanation: Custom metadata attributes in HTML5 must start with the 'data-' prefix (e.g., data-user-id).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: In JavaScript, how do you access a custom attribute declared as `data-user-role="admin"` on element `el`?
questions.explanation: Custom data-* attributes are exposed on an element's DOM `dataset` property in camelCase form (`userRole`).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which <meta> attribute specifies character encoding for the HTML document?
questions.explanation: <meta charset="UTF-8"> declares the document character encoding as UTF-8.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which meta tag prevents search engine crawlers from indexing a page?
questions.explanation: The meta robots tag with value 'noindex' instructs web crawlers not to index the page.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTTP method sends form data embedded in the URL query string?
questions.explanation: The GET method appends form input field values to the target URL query string.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which form attribute and value must be set to upload files via `<input type="file">`?
questions.explanation: Uploading binary files requires setting form enctype to "multipart/form-data" with method="POST".

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML entity code represents the ampersand symbol (&)?
questions.explanation: The & entity escapes the ampersand character in HTML.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML entity code represents the less-than symbol (<)?
questions.explanation: The < entity escapes the less-than symbol < to prevent HTML tag misparsing.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML entity code represents the greater-than symbol (>)?
questions.explanation: The > entity escapes the greater-than symbol >.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag is used to wrap a self-contained figure, diagram, or photo along with its caption?
questions.explanation: <figure> encloses self-contained visual media, while <figcaption> provides its caption.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element represents a highlighted or marked portion of text for reference purposes?
questions.explanation: The <mark> element represents text highlighted for reference or notation purposes.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag represents machine-readable date/time values using the 'datetime' attribute?
questions.explanation: The <time> element renders human-readable dates/times with machine-readable `datetime` attributes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an inline element by default?
questions.explanation:

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Can a block-level element be nested inside an inline element like <span> in standard HTML5?

options.B: No, inline elements generally should not contain block-level elements

questions.explanation: In HTML specification, inline elements generally must not contain block-level elements.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element groups related fields and labels together inside a form with a visible border?
questions.explanation: The <fieldset> tag groups related controls in a form and can take a <legend> as title.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element defines a caption for the content of a <fieldset>?
questions.explanation: The <legend> tag provides a caption for its parent <fieldset>.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element allows defining multiple alternative media resources for <video> or <audio> elements?
questions.explanation: The <source> tag specifies alternate video/audio files so browsers can pick supported formats.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which HTML5 element provides responsive images by listing multiple image sources for different screen sizes/resolutions?
questions.explanation: The element wraps multiple tags and an fallback for responsive image swapping.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: Which keyboard attribute defines element tab focus order when navigating with the Tab key?
questions.explanation: The 'tabindex' attribute specifies sequential keyboard navigation focus order.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: What does setting `tabindex="0"` do to a non-interactive element like a <div>?

options.A: Removes it from tab order entirely
options.B: Makes it focusable in natural document tab order
options.C: Focuses it first before all other elements

questions.explanation: tabindex="0" inserts the element into normal document keyboard tab order.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: What does setting `tabindex="-1"` do to an element?

options.A: Makes element focusable programmatically via JavaScript but removes it from sequential keyboard tabbing

questions.explanation: tabindex="-1" removes element from keyboard tab flow while remaining focusable via JS focus().

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which input type renders a slider control for selecting a number within a specified range?
questions.explanation: <input type="range"> produces a visual slider control for numeric input within bounds.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag measures a scalar value within a known range or fractional value (like disk usage)?
questions.explanation: <meter> represents a scalar measurement within a known range or fractional value.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag represents the completion progress of a task (like file upload)?
questions.explanation: The <progress> tag displays task execution progress (e.g., loading or file transfer).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element specifies expanding/collapsing details that user can view or hide?
questions.explanation: <details> creates an interactive disclosure widget, with <summary> as its visible heading.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which element represents a key-value list of terms and descriptions in HTML?
questions.explanation: <dl> defines a description list, containing terms (<dt>) and descriptions (<dd>).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which global attribute specifies text direction for element content (e.g., left-to-right vs right-to-left)?
questions.explanation: The 'dir' attribute specifies text directionality (ltr, rtl, auto).

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What happens if you open an tag inside a tag but close them as `Text`?

options.A: Browser HTML parser auto-corrects overlapping tags in DOM, but it is invalid syntax

questions.explanation: HTML parsers handle malformed overlapping tags via error recovery, but it violates standard syntax rules.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which <link> attribute specifies canonical URL to eliminate duplicate content SEO penalties?
questions.explanation: <link rel="canonical" href="..."> indicates preferred master page URL for search indexing.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Where does the browser construct the DOM tree from?

options.B: From tokenized raw HTML byte streams

questions.explanation: Browsers convert raw network bytes -> characters -> tokens -> nodes -> DOM Tree.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What is the purpose of the `rel="noopener noreferrer"` attribute on external target="_blank" links?

options.A: Prevents target page from accessing window.opener DOM object and protects against tabnabbing phishing attacks
options.D: Hides anchor text from search engines

questions.explanation: rel="noopener" prevents foreign cross-origin target pages from controlling window.opener object.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which attribute on <form> specifies where to send submitted form data?
questions.explanation: The 'action' attribute specifies target URI where form data payload is transmitted.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: What is a `<noscript>` tag used for?

options.A: Defines fallback content displayed to users who have disabled JavaScript or use non-scripting browsers

questions.explanation: <noscript> renders HTML content when script execution is disabled or unsupported.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag defines preformatted text where whitespace, indents, and line breaks are preserved exactly as typed?
questions.explanation: The <pre> tag renders text in monospace font, maintaining all whitespace and line breaks.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag represents inline computer code snippet?
questions.explanation: The <code> tag marks up computer source code snippets inline.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.question: Which tag represents keyboard key input (e.g. Ctrl + C) in HTML?
questions.explanation: The <kbd> tag represents keyboard input or user shortcuts.

questions.subject: HTML
questions.topic: Accessibility, ARIA basics, and alt text
questions.question: Which ARIA attribute hides an decorative or redundant element completely from accessibility screen readers?
questions.explanation: aria-hidden="true" removes an element and its children from accessibility tree.
